name: Igoumenitsa
title: Igoumenitsa Ferry UTM | Ship Thickness Gauging in Epirus
description: Thickness gauging at Igoumenitsa for Italy-route ro-pax ferries, Corfu ferries and freight ro-ro ships: vehicle deck, ramp, ballast tank and hull UTM.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for Ferries Calling at Igoumenitsa
intro: Igoumenitsa, on the Epirus coast opposite Corfu, is where the Egnatia motorway meets the Adriatic ferry lines, so its quays handle a steady flow of lorries bound for Italy as well as the busy ferries to Corfu. Calls by the big Italy-route ro-pax ships are often brief, while the Corfu ferries turn round all day, so planning decides how much gauging gets done here. For each job we bring technicians from India and fit the work into layovers, lay days and the winter timetable.

highlights.p: Smaller ferries cross between Igoumenitsa and Corfu many times a day, several of them with open vehicle decks exposed to spray and heavy lorry traffic. Gauging decks, ramps, ballast tanks and hull framing fits best into overnight stops or quieter winter days.

highlights.h: Short calls on the Italy routes
highlights.p: Many Adriatic ro-pax ferries stop at Igoumenitsa only long enough to discharge and load before continuing south or back to Italy. Lines that terminate here, and lay days built into rotations, give the longer windows that tank gauging needs.

The motorway east to Thessaloniki and the Balkans feeds lorries and trailers onto the Italy ferries. That freight is what wears vehicle-deck plating, lashing points and ramp structure, the areas a measured survey on these ships should cover first.

port.h: Igoumenitsa: Epirus ferry port at the end of the Egnatia corridor
p: Igoumenitsa sits in a sheltered bay on the Epirus coast of north-western Greece, facing the island of Corfu across a narrow stretch of the Ionian Sea, with the Albanian border a short distance to the north. The town grew as a port, and its role was transformed when the Egnatia motorway connected it with Ioannina, Thessaloniki and the border crossings into the Balkans and Turkey. Lorries that once crossed Greece on slower roads now reach the Adriatic ferries here directly. The Igoumenitsa Port Authority operates a large modern terminal for the international lines, with ro-pax berths, linkspans and marshalling yards, and keeps separate berths for the domestic ferries to Corfu and the nearby islands. Approaches from the Ionian are short and open, with no locks or bars to wait for.

Two fleets share the port. The international ro-pax ferries link Igoumenitsa with Ancona, Bari, Brindisi and Venice; most call here on rotations that continue to or from Patras, while some lines turn round at Igoumenitsa itself. They carry heavy goods vehicles, trailers, cars and passengers throughout the year, with summer adding holiday traffic. The domestic fleet is smaller and busier: ferries shuttling to Corfu town and to Lefkimmi in the south of the island, and services to Paxi, each making several crossings a day in season. These are mostly smaller ro-pax vessels, several of them with open or partly open vehicle decks. Coastal cargo ships, fishing vessels and yachts complete the picture, and between them the two fleets keep the quays busy from early morning until late at night.

The bay is protected by the coast and by Corfu, but winter storms from the south and south-west can still disturb the strait and occasionally delay sailings, and heavy rain is a feature of the Epirus winter. Summer is calm and busy, and tides are negligible. For inspection, the rhythm of the port matters more than the weather. International ferries spend a short, fixed time alongside, Corfu ferries turn round quickly through the day, and operators take ships out of service mainly in the winter months for dockings and refits elsewhere. The practical windows are therefore overnight stops, scheduled lay days, the quieter winter timetable, and periods when a ferry is held in port between charters or before being redeployed.

There is no shipyard at Igoumenitsa, so all gauging here is done afloat. On the international ferries, the work takes place at the ro-pax berths while vehicles are off: vehicle-deck plating and stiffeners, internal and stern ramps, shell door surrounds, mooring decks and the structure beneath lashing points. On a ship whose line terminates here, or which spends a lay day in port, ballast tanks and voids can be added if the crew empties and certifies them. Corfu ferries are best gauged during their overnight stop or on a quieter winter day, when the vessel can be held at its berth for a few hours without breaking the island link.

When steel renewal is needed, the ships leave. International ferries usually dock in Attica, at Perama, Salamina or the Elefsina bay, or at yards in Italy or further afield chosen by their operators, and the domestic ferries go to whichever yards their owners use. Gauging at Igoumenitsa beforehand gives the operator a measured scope to send ahead, and lets the yard prepare plate and labour so the refit fits the winter window. For lorry-heavy ferries, readings on the main freight deck taken over successive calls also show how fast wastage is progressing, which helps decide whether a deck can wait for the next docking or needs attention now.
list: International ro-pax berths: vehicle deck, ramp, shell door and lashing-point gauging while the ferry is discharged
Terminating-line and lay-day berths: longer scopes with ballast tanks, voids and shell framing from inside
Domestic ferry berths: deck, ramp and tank gauging on Corfu and Paxi ferries during overnight stops or winter lay-ups
Igoumenitsa bay anchorage: condition and pre-purchase gauging by launch on vessels waiting off the port

context.h: Ferry inspection rules and the Corfu link
p: Igoumenitsa falls under the Paris MoU, with port state control and harbour supervision exercised by the Hellenic Coast Guard through the Igoumenitsa harbour master. The international ro-pax ferries are subject to EU host-state inspections for ro-pax ships in regular service, and the domestic ferries to Corfu and Paxi are surveyed by the Greek flag administration and their class under EU standards for passenger ships on domestic voyages. Ships calling at EU ports must carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, and the Italy routes count as EU voyages for the Emissions Trading System and FuelEU Maritime.

The Corfu link is a lifeline for the island as well as a tourist route, so its ferries carry fuel trucks, supply lorries and construction traffic alongside holiday cars, and they run in every season. Open vehicle decks on some of these ships are wetted by rain and sea spray on every crossing, and their deck plating, coamings and drainage arrangements corrode faster than the enclosed decks of larger ferries. Operators deciding whether to keep or replace these ships need measured data on decks, ballast tanks and hull framing to judge how much life is left. The international ferries face a different pressure: freight from the Egnatia corridor keeps their decks loaded, and they must stay on schedule to keep the hauliers' business.

jobs.p: Requests at Igoumenitsa come from two directions. Operators of the Italy-route ferries want vehicle decks, ramps and tanks measured during calls and lay days, building a steel scope for the next refit without missing a sailing. Owners of the domestic ferries want condition data on smaller, hard-worked ships, usually during overnight stops or the winter. Buyers looking at a ferry held in port between deployments bring pre-purchase work. Each plan is agreed with the operator and master so that gauging fits the timetable, starting with the structure that matters most, and results are sent area by area so the next call's scope can be adjusted. Typical scopes:
list: Open vehicle deck, ramp and drainage area gauging on a Corfu shuttle ferry over two overnight stops in the winter timetable.
Main freight deck and lashing-point gauging on an Italy-route ro-pax ferry during a lay day, with readings compared against the previous survey.
Ballast tank and void-space gauging on a ferry whose Brindisi line terminates at Igoumenitsa, ahead of a winter docking in Attica.
Magnetic particle checks at bow door or stern-ramp hinge foundations on an international ferry, together with gauging of the adjacent plating.
Pre-purchase condition gauging on a small ferry held in port between charters, covering deck, hull framing and tanks.

logistics: Ioannina and Preveza (Aktion) airports are the closest mainland arrival points, with onward travel by road, and Corfu airport is across the strait by ferry; Athens and Thessaloniki give more international connections, with a longer road journey. The international terminal is an ISPS-controlled area, so the operator or the ship's agent arranges passes and boarding with the technicians' certificates and equipment lists. Technicians travel from India on Schengen visas. Because ferry lay days are usually fixed well ahead, we tie the visa application to the operator's published schedule.
vessels: Domestic ferries to Corfu and Paxi

faqs.q: International ferries stop only briefly at Igoumenitsa. Is gauging realistic?
faqs.a: During a short transit call, only a small scope, usually a section of vehicle deck or a ramp, and only if the operator agrees. The realistic windows are lay days, lines that terminate here, and periods when the ship is held in port. Many operators instead split the work between Igoumenitsa and Patras or the Italian port on the same rotation.

faqs.q: Can Corfu ferries be gauged without interrupting the island service?
faqs.a: Yes, by using the overnight stop or a winter day when the timetable allows one ship to be held. On these smaller ferries, the vehicle deck, ramps, drainage areas, ballast tanks and hull framing can usually be covered over one or two such windows. The operator decides which sailings can be released, and we plan the sequence so the ship is ready for its next crossing.

faqs.q: Why do open vehicle decks need particular attention?
faqs.a: Because they are wetted by rain and spray on every crossing and rarely dry out fully, while lorry tyres wear away the coating. Corrosion concentrates in deck plating near the drains, at the junction with coamings and side structure, and around lashing points. Measured readings show whether wastage is general or local, which decides between patch repairs and renewing deck plating at the next docking.

faqs.q: Can the same mobilisation include ships in Patras or Albanian ports?
faqs.a: Patras is reached by motorway and is often combined with Igoumenitsa on the same rotation. Albanian ports such as Vlorë and Durrës are close geographically but lie outside the Schengen area, and Albania has its own entry rules, which we check for each technician. Tell us early if a programme includes Albanian calls, so travel and entry can be planned together.
